scope: Independent adversarial implementation review; private fixtures only; no maintained mutations.

findings.summary: Writers check symlinks but accept an existing hard link on the mutation target, causing unrelated linked files to be overwritten.
findings.reproduction: Create a second hard link to the exact permitted source YAML or canonical TSV in a private fixture, invoke normal --apply, and observe success with both paths changed to identical new bytes. Native guarded YAML validation does not protect filesystem alias scope.
findings.expected: Reject nonregular/aliased mutation targets and recheck the actual target and inputs at the write boundary; preserve unrelated link bytes. Cover hard links and aliases introduced after reservation. Assess the new policy manifest writer for the same direct-write pattern.

findings.summary: Publication rechecks canonical/owner only, then hashes a fresh unvalidated generation manifest for the receipt.
findings.reproduction: After the real receipt reservation yields, replace manifest contents with source_revisions.claw all-zero and external_sssom_validation FAILED. Publisher returns success, changes canonical, and writes native_manifest_sha256 equal to this unverified replacement rather than the validated capture.
findings.expected: Capture immutable candidate/manifest bytes and identities, recheck all evidence inputs before mutation and after publication, and record exactly the validated hash. Add late-manifest/candidate drift regressions; no success receipt on drift.
